literal_meaning: কৃষ্ণের লীলা (Krishna's divine play or antics)
figurative_meaning_en: Illicit or forbidden relationship (used in a mocking or derogatory sense)
example_sentences_in_bangla: তাদের সম্পর্কটা তো কেষ্টলীলা, সবাই জানে।
সে তার বন্ধুর স্ত্রীর সাথে কেষ্টলীলা শুরু করেছে।
example_sentences_in_english: Their relationship is nothing but Keshto-leela; everyone knows it's improper.
He has started an illicit affair with his friend's wife, pure Keshto-leela.
history: উৎস: আয়ান ঘোষের ভাগনে শ্রীকৃষ্ণ ও পত্নী রাধার মামী-ভাগনের অবৈধসম্পর্ক (Source: The illicit aunt-nephew relationship between Shri Krishna, nephew of Ayan Ghosh, and Radha, his maternal uncle's wife, as a satirical twist on Vaishnava mythology)
note: This idiom draws from Bengali folklore and Vaishnava traditions, using 'Keshto' as a colloquial diminutive for Krishna to add a folksy, mocking tone.
